auxiliary_material: The authors hypothesize that these dietary interventions will promote intestinal microbial signatures that enhance antitumor immunity and modulate the occurrence and frequency of immune-related adverse events (irAEs). The proposal outlines a multi-omics approach to link microbiome changes with immune and metabolic parameters, though no outcome data is provided in the supplied text.

useful_material: This study describes a proposed prospective dietary intervention clinical trial design targeting melanoma patients treated with immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICI). The authors plan to implement a sequential intervention involving a high-fermented food diet followed by high-fiber supplementation. The study aims to longitudinally assess gut microbial signatures and evaluate distinct immunological, proteomic, and metabolomic effects associated with these dietary modifications.
